symptoms: Chest tightness or pressure, pain spreading to arm/jaw/back, shortness of breath during exertion, fatigue, dizziness
guidance: Often triggered by physical activity or stress and relieved by rest. Risk factors include high blood pressure, diabetes, smoking, family history. Requires ECG and cardiac evaluation. If pain is severe, sudden, or at rest, treat as emergency.

symptoms: Palpitations, fluttering or pounding heart, dizziness, fatigue, shortness of breath, fainting
guidance: Can range from harmless to life-threatening. An ECG or Holter monitor is typically needed. Fainting episodes warrant urgent evaluation.

symptoms: Often asymptomatic; may include headache, blurred vision, chest discomfort, nosebleeds in severe cases
guidance: Silent condition usually found on routine checkup. Severe hypertension with headache or vision changes needs urgent care.

symptoms: Wheezing, shortness of breath, chest tightness, coughing especially at night or with exercise
guidance: Triggered by allergens, exercise, cold air, or stress. Inhaler use should be assessed. Severe attacks with blue lips need emergency care.

symptoms: Cough with phlegm, fever, chills, difficulty breathing, chest pain when breathing or coughing, fatigue
guidance: Bacterial or viral lung infection. Requires chest X-ray and possibly antibiotics. High fever with breathing difficulty is urgent.

symptoms: Chronic cough, mucus production, wheezing, breathlessness with activity, chest tightness
guidance: Commonly linked to smoking history. Progressive condition needing pulmonary function tests and long-term management.

symptoms: Throbbing one-sided headache, nausea, sensitivity to light and sound, visual aura, can last hours to days
guidance: Common neurological condition. Sudden 'worst headache of life' or headache with confusion/weakness needs emergency evaluation for stroke.

symptoms: Numbness, tingling, burning sensation in hands or feet, muscle weakness, sensitivity to touch
guidance: Often related to diabetes, vitamin deficiency, or nerve compression. Needs neurological exam and possibly nerve conduction studies.

symptoms: Recurrent seizures, loss of consciousness, convulsions, staring spells, confusion after episodes
guidance: Requires EEG and neurology workup. An active seizure happening now is a medical emergency.

symptoms: Heartburn, regurgitation, chest discomfort after eating, sour taste, worse when lying down
guidance: Common and usually manageable with diet changes and medication. Persistent chest pain should be distinguished from cardiac causes.

symptoms: Burning stomach pain, bloating, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, dark stools if bleeding
guidance: Often caused by H. pylori infection or NSAID use. Black/bloody stools or vomiting blood needs urgent care.

symptoms: Abdominal cramping, bloating, alternating diarrhea and constipation, relief after bowel movement
guidance: Functional gut disorder, diagnosis of exclusion. Chronic symptoms warrant evaluation to rule out other conditions.

symptoms: Dull or sharp pain in lower back, stiffness, muscle spasm, pain radiating to leg if nerve involved
guidance: Most cases improve with rest, physiotherapy. Numbness, weakness, or loss of bladder control needs urgent evaluation.

symptoms: Joint pain and stiffness, especially knees/hips, worse with activity, swelling, reduced range of motion
guidance: Degenerative joint condition common with age. Managed with physiotherapy, pain relief, sometimes surgery.

symptoms: Sudden pain after injury, swelling, bruising, inability to bear weight or move the joint normally
guidance: Needs X-ray to confirm. Visible deformity or inability to move the limb requires urgent imaging.

symptoms: Itchy, red, inflamed skin patches, dryness, sometimes oozing or crusting
guidance: Chronic inflammatory skin condition. Managed with moisturizers and topical treatments.

symptoms: Itchy red rash with defined edges, scaling, sometimes ring-shaped pattern
guidance: Common and treatable with antifungal creams. Spreading rapidly or affecting large areas needs evaluation.

condition: Common Cold / Viral Upper Respiratory Infection
symptoms: Runny nose, sore throat, mild cough, sneezing, low-grade fever, fatigue
guidance: Usually self-limiting, resolves in 7-10 days. Supportive care recommended.

symptoms: Sudden fever, body aches, chills, fatigue, dry cough, headache
guidance: More severe than common cold. Antivirals may help if started early. High-risk patients should seek care promptly.

symptoms: Facial pain or pressure, nasal congestion, thick nasal discharge, reduced sense of smell, headache
guidance: Can be viral or bacterial. Persistent symptoms beyond 10 days may need antibiotics.

symptoms: Ear pain, hearing difficulty, fluid drainage, fever, irritability in children
guidance: Common in children. Severe pain with high fever needs prompt evaluation.

symptoms: Red eye, itching, discharge, gritty feeling, watery or crusty eyelids
guidance: Often viral or bacterial, highly contagious. Vision loss or severe pain needs urgent ophthalmology referral.

symptoms: Excessive worry, restlessness, difficulty concentrating, muscle tension, sleep disturbance
guidance: Common mental health condition, very treatable with therapy and/or medication. Persistent symptoms affecting daily life warrant evaluation.

symptoms: Persistent sadness, loss of interest, fatigue, sleep or appetite changes, difficulty concentrating
guidance: Treatable with therapy and/or medication. Any mention of self-harm or suicidal thoughts requires immediate crisis support.

symptoms: Burning urination, frequent urge to urinate, cloudy or strong-smelling urine, pelvic discomfort
guidance: Common, especially in women. Fever and back pain may indicate kidney involvement and need urgent care.

symptoms: Sudden high fever, severe headache, pain behind the eyes, joint and muscle pain, rash, nausea, low platelet count
guidance: Mosquito-borne viral infection, common in India especially during/after monsoon. Needs CBC/platelet monitoring. Bleeding gums, persistent vomiting, severe abdominal pain, or drop in platelets requires urgent hospital care (risk of dengue hemorrhagic fever).

symptoms: Cyclical high fever with chills and sweating, headache, body ache, fatigue, nausea, vomiting
guidance: Mosquito-borne parasitic infection, common in India. Diagnosed via blood smear/rapid test. High fever with confusion, repeated vomiting, or jaundice needs urgent evaluation (possible severe/cerebral malaria).

symptoms: Sustained high fever (often worse in evening), abdominal pain, weakness, headache, loss of appetite, sometimes constipation or diarrhea, rose-colored rash
guidance: Bacterial infection from contaminated food/water, common in India. Needs blood culture or Widal test. Severe abdominal pain or signs of intestinal bleeding/perforation needs emergency care.

symptoms: Sudden vomiting, watery diarrhea, abdominal cramps, nausea, sometimes fever, dehydration
guidance: Usually viral or bacterial, often self-limiting in 1-3 days with hydration. Signs of severe dehydration (dizziness, very dark urine, no urination, sunken eyes), blood in stool, or high fever needs urgent evaluation, especially in children and elderly.

symptoms: Increased thirst, frequent urination, fatigue, blurred vision, slow-healing wounds, unexplained weight loss
guidance: Common metabolic condition, often gradual onset. Diagnosed via fasting glucose/HbA1c. Confusion, fruity-smelling breath, rapid breathing, or very high/low blood sugar with symptoms needs emergency care (possible DKA or severe hypoglycemia).

symptoms: Fatigue, weight gain, cold intolerance, dry skin, hair thinning, constipation, depression, slowed heart rate
guidance: Common, especially in women. Diagnosed via TSH blood test. Gradual onset condition managed with thyroid hormone replacement and monitoring.

symptoms: Weight loss despite normal appetite, rapid heartbeat, sweating, heat intolerance, tremor, anxiety, bulging eyes
guidance: Diagnosed via TSH/T3/T4 blood tests. Rapid heart rate with chest pain or severe agitation needs urgent evaluation (possible thyroid storm).

symptoms: Severe one-sided flank or back pain that comes in waves, pain radiating to groin, blood in urine, nausea, vomiting, painful urination
guidance: Common condition requiring imaging (ultrasound/CT) to confirm. Pain combined with fever and chills suggests infection and needs urgent care. Inability to urinate is an emergency.

symptoms: Frequent urination especially at night, weak urine stream, difficulty starting urination, feeling of incomplete emptying
guidance: Common in older men. Complete inability to urinate (urinary retention) is an emergency requiring immediate care.

symptoms: Cramping lower abdominal pain during periods, lower back pain, nausea, fatigue
guidance: Very common. Usually manageable with pain relief and heat. Severe pain that disrupts daily life, or pain with heavy/irregular bleeding, warrants gynecological evaluation.

symptoms: Irregular periods, weight gain, acne, excess facial/body hair, difficulty conceiving
guidance: Common hormonal condition, diagnosed via clinical evaluation, ultrasound and bloodwork. Managed long-term with lifestyle changes and medication.

condition: Vaginal / Urinary Tract Infection in Women
symptoms: Pelvic discomfort, unusual discharge, itching, burning during urination, odor
guidance: Common and treatable. Fever, severe pelvic pain, or back pain may indicate a more serious infection requiring urgent care.

symptoms: Missed period, nausea, breast tenderness, fatigue, spotting
guidance: Confirm with a pregnancy test and obstetric evaluation. Heavy bleeding, severe abdominal pain, or fainting during pregnancy is an emergency.

symptoms: Fever, fussiness, reduced appetite, mild cough or runny nose, lethargy
guidance: Common in children, usually viral. Fever above 40°C, a child who is difficult to wake, a rash that doesn't fade under pressure, or signs of dehydration needs urgent pediatric evaluation.

symptoms: Ear pain or pulling at ear, fever, irritability, difficulty sleeping, reduced hearing
guidance: Common in young children. Persistent high fever or fluid draining from the ear needs prompt evaluation.

symptoms: Mouth sores, rash on hands and feet, mild fever, reduced appetite, irritability in young children
guidance: Common, contagious viral illness in children, usually mild and self-limiting. Refusal to drink fluids or signs of dehydration needs evaluation.

symptoms: Pimples, blackheads, whiteheads, oily skin, occasional cysts, mostly on face/back/chest
guidance: Very common, especially in teens and young adults. Managed with topical/oral treatments. Severe cystic acne or scarring warrants dermatology referral.

symptoms: Itchy raised red welts on skin that can move/change location, mild swelling
guidance: Often allergic in origin. Usually resolves with antihistamines. If accompanied by facial/throat swelling or breathing difficulty, treat as anaphylaxis emergency.

symptoms: Intense itching especially at night, small red bumps or burrows, often between fingers, wrists, waistline
guidance: Contagious skin infestation requiring topical treatment and household-level precautions. Close contacts should be evaluated too.

symptoms: Throat pain, difficulty swallowing, redness, sometimes fever and swollen glands
guidance: Usually viral, sometimes bacterial (strep). Severe difficulty swallowing or breathing, or drooling in a child, needs urgent evaluation.

symptoms: Severe sore throat, swollen tonsils sometimes with white patches, fever, difficulty swallowing, bad breath
guidance: Can be viral or bacterial. Recurrent episodes may need ENT evaluation. Difficulty breathing or swallowing saliva needs urgent care.

symptoms: Brief spinning sensation triggered by head movement, nausea, imbalance
guidance: Common inner-ear condition, often resolves with repositioning maneuvers. Vertigo with slurred speech, weakness, or persistent severe symptoms needs urgent neurological evaluation to rule out stroke.

symptoms: Gritty or burning sensation, redness, sensitivity to light, blurred vision that improves with blinking
guidance: Common, often related to screen use or environment. Managed with lubricating drops. Persistent symptoms warrant an eye exam.

symptoms: Painful red bump on eyelid margin, swelling, tenderness, occasionally discharge
guidance: Usually resolves with warm compresses. Spreading redness, vision changes, or significant swelling needs evaluation.

symptoms: Sudden blurred or lost vision, eye pain, flashes of light, curtain-like shadow in vision, eye injury
guidance: Sudden vision changes or eye trauma are time-sensitive emergencies — same-day or immediate ophthalmology evaluation is needed to prevent permanent vision loss.

symptoms: Sudden intense fear, racing heart, chest tightness, shortness of breath, dizziness, trembling, fear of dying
guidance: Common and treatable, though symptoms can closely mimic a heart attack. First episode with chest pain should be medically evaluated to rule out cardiac causes before assuming panic attack.

symptoms: Difficulty falling or staying asleep, waking too early, daytime fatigue, irritability, difficulty concentrating
guidance: Common, often linked to stress, anxiety, or habits. Persistent insomnia affecting daily function warrants evaluation.

symptoms: Fatigue, pale skin, weakness, shortness of breath on exertion, dizziness, brittle nails, cold hands/feet
guidance: Common, especially in menstruating women and vegetarians. Diagnosed via CBC and iron studies. Severe fatigue with chest pain or fainting needs urgent evaluation.

symptoms: Sneezing, runny or itchy nose, watery itchy eyes, congestion, no fever
guidance: Common, often seasonal or trigger-related. Managed with antihistamines and trigger avoidance. Distinguish from infection by the absence of fever.

symptoms: Gradual shoulder stiffness and pain, significantly reduced range of motion, worse at night
guidance: Develops over weeks to months. Managed with physiotherapy; sometimes requires injections. More common with diabetes.

symptoms: Throbbing tooth pain, sensitivity to hot/cold, swelling of gum or face, pain when chewing
guidance: Needs dental evaluation; may indicate cavity, abscess, or cracked tooth. Facial swelling spreading toward the eye or throat, fever, or difficulty swallowing/breathing needs emergency care (risk of spreading infection).
